Tripling LLM benchmark performance no longer requires retraining, just the right API configuration.

As developers, we often look for complex solutions when simple optimizations of our existing systems can yield the most significant results.

Here are the key technical developments in AI and security from the last 24 hours:

🚀 OpenAI tripled its GPT-5.6 performance scores on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark simply by enabling two specific API settings designed to retain reasoning and enable compaction.

🛡️ Anthropic is currently identifying software vulnerabilities faster than Microsoft can patch them, forcing Microsoft into a behind-the-scenes dash to fix exploits before hackers find them.

🔐 The HAWK cryptographic algorithm, a third-round post-quantum cryptography candidate that withstood years of testing, has been taken out of commission by a newly discovered vulnerability called the Mythos attack.

💻 Google has expanded the desktop utility of Gemini for macOS by adding new natural language capabilities directly to the platform.

These updates show that the engineering landscape is shifting. Success is no longer just about model scale, but about how we optimize API calls, manage inference efficiency, and secure our infrastructure against novel automated threats.

Are you focusing more on optimizing API configurations like compaction, or are you still relying primarily on default model settings for your production pipelines?
